On July 28th, I took my two pets for a bath, and then a few hours later they called to inform me that they were going to sedate my pet because she wouldn't cooperate, and that it would cost $100 more than the $220 I had already paid. I accepted the sedation. Later, I called to check on my pets and they told me they were doing great, which reassured me. Then, a few hours later, they called again and told me they were ready. I went immediately to pick them up, and to my surprise, my female dog smelled like death and had all her fur and nails matted. My male dog was exactly as I had brought them; they hadn't done anything to him at all, except that he smelled awful. They told me to bring them back the next day to be bathed again, but I started calling the manager of the place and she never answered. I decided to go in person, and she told me to bring them back the next day to be bathed again and that she would refund me $100 and give it to the vet because my female dog had arrived with a... She had a cut on her paw and was limping, and they told me to bring them back in a month and they wouldn't charge me. So the next day I went at 8 am because I thought the manager was serious, but when I arrived I was told she wasn't there and they didn't know what time I'd be there, and she wasn't answering her phone. They told me to forget about the person who bathes the pets that day, but before that they made me sign some documents and took me to a room where they told me the vet was coming. After a few minutes, they told me they weren't going to see me. I left the room and asked for my pets back because they had taken them to cages, I don't know why. The manager herself said they bathe them and then put them in those cages, and they come out smelling like weeds. I don't understand why they put them in there if they bathe them. Anyway, I left that place without them doing anything to my pets and I started calling that manager so they would answer me, and they gave me back the 220, but my My pets are now being treated like dirt, and I don't know what diseases they caught there. I'm going to expose on social media and in groups how dishonest this veterinary clinic is, and above all, warn people not to take their pets to this so-called clinic where all they do is charge for everything. It's a miracle they don't charge us for air and sunlight because they don't know how to do it. Besides, the cleanliness is terrible. I took them there because I don't know any other place and I don't know the addresses here, but this clinic is awful, and the people who work there are liars, just like the manager. My pets are very sick; I don't know what they caught. I beg people who take their pets there to be very careful and not have what happened to me happen to them. Now I have to take them to another vet to be cured. Look at how my pet looks, and they still claim they cut his hair, and look how the infection is spreading. I'm reporting this so it doesn't happen to your pets, and I want to clarify that they refunded my money because I told them I was going to report these events. They charged me for something they didn't do, and that's how they refunded my money. But now I have to take her to get it fixed, and I don't know how much it's going to cost. I hope they don't delete this post.
They only allow comments they pay people to post because nothing they say is true. Their so-called good service is a lie; it's terrible service.

I came in looking for help and guidance regarding my dog’s situation, but instead I left feeling stressed, unheard, and without a clear solution. Dr. Andrea Zanetti communication style was not what I expected from a veterinary professional. I felt that he was dismissive and rude when addressing my concerns.

I was looking for professional advice, reassurance, and a plan to help my dog improve. Instead, I left the appointment feeling more anxious and with unresolved concerns.

I brought my young dog in for vaccines and honestly I was confused with how the visit went.

What confused me was that I initially believed my dog might have loose stool, which is why we discussed postponing vaccines. I was completely fine with that if he actually had diarrhea. However, I showed the doctor a photo of my dog’s stool during the appointment, and the doctor specifically told me that it was not loose stool and that my dog appeared fine. Despite that, we still left without the vaccines I had scheduled the visit for.

During the same visit, the doctor suggested $1,000 in pancreatic testing, along with other tests and X-rays, even though he had just said the stool looked normal and that my dog appeared healthy. That's totally inconsistent with what I was just told. If the stool was normal and my dog was fine, it was difficult for me to understand why the vaccines could not be completed as planned and why he needed testing.

I did not decline care, the doctor told me the stool was not loose and that my dog was fine, but the conversation then shifted to expensive testing and imaging rather than completing the vaccines I had come in for.

The front desk staff and nursing team at this clinic are absolutely wonderful, kind, helpful, and really accommodating. The clinic itself has a classic, old-school vet vibe, and you can tell they know what they’re doing. I would absolutely recommend the clinic overall.
However, my experience with Dr. Andrea Zanetti was extremely disappointing. He was dismissive, and condescending from the moment he walked in. He didn’t make eye contact once during the entire consultation, barely spoke while examining my dog, and when I asked questions to clarify what was being prescribed, he abruptly told me to “hang on” and left the room, never came back.
Instead, a nurse returned with a highly inflated quote of nearly $900. I had to ask her to walk me through every line item to understand what was being recommended, and it turned out a good portion of it wasn’t even necessary.
I never saw Dr. Zanetti again, and at no point did he bother to explain anything or ensure I understood the treatment plan. That kind of lack of basic communication and respect, especially in a stressful situation, is not acceptable.
So, 4 stars because the clinic and team (apart from Dr. Zanetti) were lovely, but I would not recommend seeing this particular vet.

I told them he needed extractions. They said he just needed a cleaning but they would let me know if he needed extractions and charged me over $1000 for the "teeth cleaning" and some medicine. I put quotations because I don't think they did anything. My cat had the same dental issues after the treatment at Green's. Additionally, when I went to pick him up and him home, they had JUST woken him up so he was really high on the medicine and could not come down for several hours. He continued to be lethargic and drooling(I went to a different vet for a second opinion and they told me my cat has stomatitis, rotten and fractured teeth, and SEVERAL ABSCESSES --ALL of which had been there during the treatment at Green's. And when my cat came home from the new vet, they woke him up hours before pickup time so he was fine when he got home.) My cat was in a lot of pain and Green's Dog and Cat Hospital treated it like a joke. It's simply a cash grab and I'm out $1000+ because I trusted them to correctly care for my cat and they took advantage of me. Note: my family had gone to them for DECADES for all of our pets, but this was the last straw. I'm disgusting with them and will no longer send my pets there. The last time we were there, we complained to the business about their lack of professionalism and how they didn't do their jobs to relieve my cat of his pain, and even asked why they didn't extract his rotten teeth, and the doctor shrugged. Last year, I took my dog there as she started limping, and she had a growth on her face. They told me regarding her limping that she had severe arthritis and prescribed me medication that never actually worked. This had started for about 4 to 5 months. They had given me different medications some stronger than others for her. She became very ill and had started swelling. I had to end up, rushing her to a hospital on a Sunday. only to find out, she had a tumor that had ruptured, and the tumor was as big as her abdomen with all the x-rays and the examinations she had had here at green dog and cat. I cannot understand how they ever missed a tumor. The only thing I think they’re good for is giving shots other issues need to be taken to a better veterinarian or hospital. I went to this hospital to vaccinate my dog, but when she goes to the vet she gets a little aggressive, so it’s common for veterinarians to take their time with her. This time, though, when the vet came to the office and saw that she was a little aggressive, he quickly put a leash on her neck and tightened it while holding her neck down. The anxiety of being held down, paired with what I presume to be trouble breathing, she began to hyperventilate and her eyes looked like they were protruding. I sat there paralyzed not knowing what to do, stammering and in shock at what the vet was doing to my dog literally in front of me as though it were standard protocol. My dog ended up defecating and urinating on the table from the anxiety, after which she was finally ‘subdued’, as the vet put it. All that just to put a stethoscope on her belly and leave. I have never had such a horrible experience with a vet—if your dog isn’t good with the vet and requires some patience, be wary of doctor A. Zanetti. Now my poor baby is traumatized and with all the love we give her at home, that must have been something hard for her. She's not used to anything close to that kind of treatment.
